chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Arrogance is that you belittle the people and consider the Truth as foolish.

key_terms.تَغْمِصَ: To belittle, to despise, to look down upon

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this concise definition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that distinguishes arrogance as an active internal disposition—'disliking' (ghumṣ) others and 'deeming foolish' (safah) the truth—rather than just external behavior. This dual mechanism explains how pride corrupts both social relations and intellectual humility, a concept central to Shia ethical theology. The hadith serves as a diagnostic tool for self-reflection, linking the rejection of divine guidance directly to the ego's dismissal of others' worth.
